data.exact_reserve_text: The Syndicate recorded an underwriting loss before investment income of GBP 6.6m (2020: GBP 40.2m loss), mainly driven by an improvement in underwriting performance and the RITC of 2018 and prior years of account.

prior_year_events.impact_description: decrease of claims incurred due to the impact on Covid-19 in 2020 underwriting year, following review of overall provision in light of FCA's Business Interruption Test Case outcome.

prior_year_events.event_name: RITC of 2018 and prior years of account
prior_year_events.impact_description: RITC covers legacy business underwritten by the Syndicate on the 2018 and prior underwriting years, resulting in the Syndicate having only transactions relating to 2019 to 2021 underwriting years during the 2021 financial year.

named_events.loss_description: Other losses for which the Syndicate had large exposure during the year were Hurricane Ida (GBP 7.9m net)
Other losses for which the Syndicate had large exposure during the year were Hurricane Ida (GBP 7.9m net) and civil unrest in South African (GBP 2.4m net).

Throughout 2021 the COVID-19 pandemic has continued to develop although changes to policy wordings and underwriting standards have removed most direct exposure to further losses. Whilst reducing over time as claims are settled, the Syndicate's exposure to COVID-19 losses remains material and continues to be monitored closely through the quarterly reserving cycle.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate did not explicitly state a gross prior year development figure. However, the report indicates an overall improvement in underwriting performance, partly due to the RITC of 2018 and prior years of account, and a decrease in claims incurred related to the 2020 underwriting year due to COVID-19 impacts. This suggests a net release of reserves.

data.data_quality_notes: The report does not explicitly state a single gross prior year development figure for the entire syndicate. The RITC of 2018 and prior years of account significantly impacts the claims provisions, making direct calculation from movement tables difficult. The direction of 'release' is inferred from narrative text indicating 'improvement in underwriting performance' and 'decrease of claims incurred due to Covid-19 in 2020 underwriting year'. Gross premium mix is derived from the 'Segmental Information' table, which combines direct and reinsurance business for each category.
